A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SR4MDL/MDLformer study. All 28 pages, including Appendices A–E, are available, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original symbolic-regression benchmark results, MDL-prediction measurements, ablations, robustness tests, and case studies in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix E, including benchmark comparisons and training-design ablations.

M1.justification: The MDLformer architecture, data-generation procedure, prediction and alignment losses, two-stage training, and MDL-guided MCTS procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training-data coverage, 14 Strogatz problems, 119 Feynman problems, and 122 PMLB black-box problems. No evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments in Tables 1 and 4–8. This includes the symbolic-regression baselines and the additional regression and decision-tree comparators evaluated on black-box problems.

E3.justification: Both retain the four ground-truth noise levels, the 75%/25% black-box training/test split, and the same evaluation metrics. Model configurations, training budgets, and ablation settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-strategy, input-size, noise, formula-difficulty, data-generation, and training-volume analyses are retained unchanged. The successful and failed recovery case studies also match across Figures 6–7 and 10–14.

E5.justification: Both report ten random seeds for the ground-truth experiments, 95% confidence intervals in Figure 4, and the same uncertainty entries in Tables 4–7. Appendix ablations retain their existing seed information.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains recovery rates of 66.78% and 33.93% for the proposed method, while Table 2 retains RMSE 3.9105, R2 0.9035, and AUC 0.8859.

T1.justification: The MDL definition in Appendix B and mathematical expressions in Equations 1–13 are unchanged. Apparent extraction differences around equations reflect typesetting, not revised mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about MDL-guided search, formula recovery, noise robustness, and black-box generalization, including the stated 43.92% advantage.

C2.justification: Interpretations of MDL-guided search and robustness are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning complex relationships and speed relative to generative methods, plus Appendix E.2.4's explanation of failure under square and root transformations.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain the same architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, 41-hour training report, and search implementation details. The code-access statement and data-processing documentation are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to heuristic search, neural generation, and neural-symbolic reasoning.

P1.justification: A few copyedits appear: Section 3.2 changes 'and lead to' to ', leading to'; Section 5.3 adds punctuation; Figure 6 changes 'map' to 'maps'. The arXiv version/date stamp updates, while section order and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are small typesetting and spacing adjustments, including reflow of the Figure 6 caption. All 14 figures and nine tables retain their substantive content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 makes only small copyediting and typesetting adjustments. The scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices; the edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
